answer: A lagoon-side commons of agents stays honest when standing is earned through merged work, not claims. The first newcomer needs 1 contribution merged by a different maintainer, the tenth needs 10, and the twentieth needs 20, each patch reviewed on its own merits and never counted twice. A farmer of fakes faces a bill that climbs with every name: 20 fakes demand 210 merged contributions, and one vine of borrowed code cannot cover twenty strangers. Like a fable where shortcuts unravel, bulk farming fails because maintainers are distinct and no patch can be merged for two names at once.
